name: Cookiepass – Cookie Banner & Consent Mode v2
author: Cookiepass Cookie Banner Consent Team

sections.description:
Cookiepass adds a cookie consent banner to your site and holds back trackers until the visitor agrees. Every decision is stored as a verifiable consent record, and Google Consent Mode v2 is set before any Google tag fires.

Connect in one click. Click “Connect with Cookiepass”, sign in or create a free account, done. The plugin sets up your site and a standard banner with your privacy policy and imprint links. No ID to copy, no code to paste.

Features

  • Set up everything inside WordPress: design your banner, scan your site and sort your cookies without leaving the admin
  • Blocks known trackers automatically until consent is given
  • Google Consent Mode v2 – safe defaults before any Google tag loads; the visitor’s decision is passed on from the Starter plan
  • Verifiable record for every consent decision
  • Banner in the visitor’s language
  • Works with the WP Consent API (if that plugin is installed), so plugins that read it – for example Site Kit by Google – respect the visitor’s choice
  • Keeps caching and optimisation plugins (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Autoptimize, Jetpack Boost, Cloudflare Rocket Loader) from delaying the banner script
  • Design, texts and categories are managed in the Cookiepass dashboard – the same banner works on every site you run

What you need

A Cookiepass account. The free plan covers one website. You can create the account during the connection step.

The plugin is open source (GPLv2 or later). Cookiepass, the service it connects to, is a commercial service operated by PF Capital Management UG (haftungsbeschränkt).

External services

This plugin connects your site to Cookiepass (https://cookiepass.io), a consent management service operated by PF Capital Management UG (haftungsbeschränkt), Germany. Without it the plugin cannot show a banner.

  1. Banner script. On every page of your site, the visitor’s browser loads https://cdn.cookiepass.io/cp.js together with your property ID. Like any file request, this sends the visitor’s IP address and browser information to Cookiepass. The script then loads your banner configuration from Cookiepass.
  2. Consent records. When a visitor makes or changes a choice, the script sends the decision to Cookiepass: a random consent ID, the chosen categories, the banner language and version. Cookiepass stores it together with the browser’s user agent and a shortened IP address as proof of consent.
  3. Cookie list and installation check. The script reports the names of cookies and browser storage entries found on the page, so that the banner can list them, and whether the banner is installed correctly. No cookie values are sent.
  4. Connecting. When an administrator clicks “Connect with Cookiepass”, a small window opens cookiepass.io with your site’s domain, the address of the WordPress administration, the site name and, if set, the addresses of your privacy policy and imprint pages. After signing in, Cookiepass sends the window back with a one-time code.
  5. Access key. Your site sends that one-time code to cookiepass.io and receives an access key for this one website in return. The key is stored in your WordPress database (an option without autoload). It is never printed into a page, and you can end it in your Cookiepass dashboard at any time.
  6. Setup page. When an administrator opens Cookiepass in the admin menu, your WordPress server sends the key to cookiepass.io and receives a one-time entry (valid for five minutes), and with it a session token for this one website (valid for two hours, kept on your server until shortly before it ends). The setup page is part of your WordPress administration: the administrator’s browser talks only to your own WordPress, and your WordPress server talks to cookiepass.io. With the token it asks for the status of your banner, the page views of this month and your plan; loads and saves the banner design (colour, layout and the addresses of your privacy policy and imprint) in step 1; starts, follows or cancels a scan of your site, reads the cookies found and saves the category you pick for a cookie in step 2; and asks Cookiepass to check your homepage for the banner in step 3. Only the link “More options on cookiepass.io” opens Cookiepass in a new browser tab, with a fresh one-time entry; that page is loaded from Cookiepass like any website, which receives the usual connection data (IP address, browser information). With every request your WordPress server also sends the language of the administrator’s WordPress, so that messages from Cookiepass arrive in that language. When step 1 is saved, the whole banner configuration as loaded from Cookiepass (name, preset and settings) goes back with it; only the fields you changed are different.
  7. Exact preview (off by default). Only when an administrator switches on “Exact preview” in step 1: each time step 1 is opened, your WordPress server asks cookiepass.io, with the session token of point 6, for the preview data of your banner (its texts in the language of your website, the cookie categories and the cookies found on your site) and for the banner configuration. The language of your website (from the WordPress settings) is sent with it. The plugin draws the banner itself, with files included in the plugin; the administrator’s browser loads nothing from Cookiepass. Only a logo you have set in Cookiepass by web address is loaded by the browser directly from that address, as on your site. The setting is stored in your WordPress database and is not sent anywhere.
  8. Status. The widget on the dashboard asks cookiepass.io for the status of your banner and the page views of this month (the key is the only thing sent) and keeps the answer for ten minutes.

Terms of service: https://cookiepass.io/terms
Privacy policy: https://cookiepass.io/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Cookiepass in the admin menu and click “Connect with Cookiepass”.
  3. Sign in or create a free account in the small window and confirm your domain – the setup appears right inside WordPress and the banner is live.
sections.faq:
Does this work with Google Analytics, Google Ads and Tag Manager?

Yes. Cookiepass sets the Google Consent Mode v2 defaults (everything denied) before any Google tag loads – on every plan. From the Starter plan on, it also passes the visitor’s decision on to Google.

I use a caching or optimisation plugin. Do I need to change anything?

Usually not. When you connect or change settings, the plugin empties the page cache of common caching plugins so the banner shows up right away. The plugin marks its script so that WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Autoptimize, Jetpack Boost, WP Meteor and Cloudflare Rocket Loader leave it alone. If another plugin delays or combines JavaScript, exclude cdn.cookiepass.io/cp.js there.

Some trackers still load before consent.

The banner script is printed first in <head>. Scripts that a theme writes into its template before wp_head() run earlier – move them into a plugin or a tag manager, or mark them with type="text/plain" data-cookiepass="statistics" (or marketing).

Can I use it on a staging site?

Yes. Connect your live domain once and choose it when you connect the staging site. Subdomains of a connected domain work automatically.

Where do I change the design and texts?

Colour, layout and the links to your privacy policy and imprint: in WordPress under Cookiepass → Setup, step 1. Logo, texts and everything else: in the Cookiepass dashboard under “Configuration”, or with “More options on cookiepass.io” in step 1. Changes reach your site automatically; nothing needs to be updated in WordPress. Step 1 shows a simplified preview; switch on “Exact preview” there to see your real banner with its texts.

Where do I get help?

For questions about the plugin, use the support forum. For questions about your Cookiepass account, contact Cookiepass.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • New setting “Exact preview” in step 1, off by default: shows your real banner with its texts, drawn with the same template the banner uses on your site. The data come through your own WordPress server; the browser loads nothing from Cookiepass. Your own logo is shown too, also as SVG.
  • The simplified preview now follows the real banner: only the buttons your banner shows (Reject all, Allow selection, Accept all in your colour), with places for the logo and the category switches.
  • A web address that WordPress would have to change (for example because of < > or spaces) is no longer saved silently changed; the field says why.
  • “View on my site” suggests a private window: after a choice on your site the banner does not appear there again.

1.2.0

  • The setup is now part of the WordPress administration itself. Step 1 (colour, layout and the links to your privacy policy and imprint, with a preview), step 2 (scan your site, sort your cookies), step 3 (check that the banner is live) and the settings talk to Cookiepass through your own WordPress server; no page from cookiepass.io is embedded any more.
  • Your access key and the session token stay on your server; they never reach the browser.
  • Existing connections keep working after the update. There is no need to connect again.

1.1.0

  • Set up Cookiepass inside WordPress: new “Cookiepass” entry in the admin menu. Connect once in a small window, then design your banner, scan your site and sort your cookies without leaving WordPress.
  • New dashboard widget with the banner status and the page views of this month.
  • Existing connections keep working. Reconnect once to use the setup inside WordPress.

1.0.5

  • New, simpler settings screen: one green button to connect, one to customize the banner. Notes about your homepage, another cookie plugin or the domain appear only when something needs your attention.
  • The manual property ID field, the blocking setting and the Disconnect button are gone; existing connections stay as they are. To connect another domain or account, delete the plugin and install it again.

1.0.4

  • Name now says what it does: “Cookiepass – Cookie Banner & Consent Mode v2”.
  • The description states which part is open source: the plugin is, the Cookiepass service it connects to is a commercial service.

1.0.3

  • Translations are no longer bundled with the plugin; they are delivered through translate.wordpress.org.

1.0.2

  • Self-check on the settings page: the plugin loads your homepage and tells you whether the banner is really delivered – with a button to clear the page cache and check again.
  • Warns when the site runs on a different domain than the one it is connected to.
  • No banner inside page builder previews (Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen and others) and the customizer, so it never covers the editor.
  • Finds the privacy policy page by its usual address when none is selected under Settings → Privacy.
  • Themes that do not call wp_head() still get the banner.

1.0.1

  • Empties the page cache of common caching plugins (WP-Optimize, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, SiteGround Optimizer, Autoptimize and others) when you connect, disconnect or change settings, so the banner appears right away.
  • Warns when another cookie consent plugin is active, which would show a second banner.

1.0.0

  • First release: one-click connection, standard banner with your legal links, automatic blocking, Google Consent Mode v2, WP Consent API, protection against caching and optimisation plugins.

The Cookiepass entry in the admin menu: one green button connects your site.
